transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose it’s mostly that I’ve been having a hard time not thinking about how rough and worn I look. My face and my hands especially—cracks, spots, sagging, that kind of thing. I know that probably sounds vain, and my wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but when I’m around bankers or county people, I feel like they’re staring right at it. I just can’t seem to get past it.
Do these concerns about your appearance ever extend beyond your face and hands—like other parts of your body—or do they mainly stay focused on those areas?

Mostly those areas, I think… my face and my hands. That’s what I can’t seem to get past—the cracks and spots, the sagging, just looking rough and worn. Maybe that sounds a little foolish, but when I’m around bankers or county folks, I feel like that’s what they’re noticing, even though my wife says I just look like someone who’s worked outdoors.
Do these concerns about your face and hands make it hard for you to function normally—like at work, in social situations, or anywhere else?

I mean… not completely, I still get my work done for the most part. But yes, I guess it has gotten in the way some. I’ve missed calls with bankers, and I’ve put off decisions around the farm because I couldn’t quite get myself looking… acceptable enough to sit down with people.

And I’ve stopped saying yes to photos for the retreat and the craft sales, even though I know those would probably help. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it does interfere, I suppose.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, touching your face or hands, or trying to cover them up—because of how you feel about your appearance?

I guess I do some of that, yes… not in a dramatic way, I don’t think. But before I leave for a loan meeting, or if I’m going to sit at a craft-fair table, I’ll check the bathroom mirror, then the truck mirror, and sort of turn my hat this way and that to see if it helps.

And I catch myself looking at my hands too much… sometimes comparing them to the younger workers’ hands, which I know probably isn’t useful. It can eat up time I should be using on the farm. I’m not proud of that, but… yes, I suppose I do repeat those things.
Do you feel that these cracks, spots, or the way your skin looks are things that most people wouldn’t notice, but they stand out a lot to you?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I know other people probably aren’t studying me the way I feel like they are. My wife tells me I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, and maybe she’s right.

But to me, the cracks and spots on my hands, and the sagging or worn look in my face… they feel very obvious. When I’m sitting with a banker or someone from the county, it’s hard not to feel like that’s what they’re seeing first. I know that may sound a bit much, but that’s honestly what I can’t seem to get past.
